548	## Node Selection Heuristics
549	
550	Quick decision guide. For full details, read the linked plugin's `planning.md`.
551	
552	### "I need to call an external service"
553	
554	1. Is there a connector with a curated activity? Run `uip maestro flow registry list --output json` and check for typed nodes matching `uipath.connector.<key>.<operation>`. If the desired operation appears as a node type, it is a curated activity -> [connector](plugins/connector/planning.md)
555	2. Connector exists but the operation is not listed as a curated node type? -> `core.action.http.v2` connector mode — see [http](plugins/http/planning.md)
556	3. No connector exists, but has a REST API? -> `core.action.http.v2` manual mode — see [http](plugins/http/planning.md)
557	4. No API at all (desktop app, terminal)? -> [rpa](plugins/rpa/planning.md) or `core.logic.mock` if unpublished
558	
559	### "I need to branch"
560	
561	- Two paths -> [decision](plugins/decision/planning.md)
562	- Three or more paths -> [switch](plugins/switch/planning.md)
563	- Branch on HTTP response status -> [http](plugins/http/planning.md) built-in branches
564	
565	### "I need to transform data"
566	
567	- Standard map/filter/group-by -> [transform](plugins/transform/planning.md)
568	- Custom logic, string manipulation, computation -> [script](plugins/script/planning.md)
569	
570	### "I need to end the flow"
571	
572	- Normal completion -> [end](plugins/end/planning.md) (one per terminal path)
573	- Fatal error, abort everything -> [terminate](plugins/terminate/planning.md)
574	
575	### "I need to wait"
576	
577	- Fixed duration -> [delay](plugins/delay/planning.md)
578	- Wait until a specific time -> [delay](plugins/delay/planning.md)
579	- Wait for external work to complete -> [queue](plugins/queue/planning.md) (`create-and-wait`)
580	
581	### "I need human involvement"
582	
583	- Human approval or data entry -> [hitl](plugins/hitl/planning.md) or `core.logic.mock` if the app doesn't exist
584	
585	### "I need an AI agent"
586	
587	- Low-code agent tightly coupled to this flow, bundled inside the flow project -> [inline-agent](plugins/inline-agent/planning.md) (`uipath.agent.autonomous`)
588	- Coded (Python) agent, or any agent that lives as a separate project (in this solution or published to Orchestrator) -> [agent](plugins/agent/planning.md) (`uipath.core.agent.{key}`)
589	
590	### "I need an LLM to process rows of a CSV or summarize a document"
591	
592	- Add LLM-generated columns to every row of a CSV (classify, summarize, extract) -> [batch-transform](plugins/batch-transform/planning.md) (`uipath.pattern.batch-transform`)
593	- Synthesize or answer questions over one attached document, with optional citations -> [summarize](plugins/summarize/planning.md) (`uipath.pattern.deep-rag`)
594	- Small ad-hoc reshaping (map/filter/groupBy) without an LLM -> [transform](plugins/transform/planning.md)
595	- Multi-step reasoning with tool use -> [inline-agent](plugins/inline-agent/planning.md) or [agent](plugins/agent/planning.md)
596	
597	### "I need to extract structured fields from documents"
598	
599	- Source is a PDF, scanned form, photo, or email attachment with **variable layout** across inputs (invoices from many vendors, receipts, contracts, forms) -> [ixp](plugins/ixp/planning.md) (`uipath.ixp.{modelName}.{fullyQualifiedName}`)
600	- Source is already structured (CSV, JSON, database row) -> [script](plugins/script/planning.md) or [transform](plugins/transform/planning.md)
601	- Need free-form summarization, classification, or open-ended reasoning -> [agent](plugins/agent/planning.md) or [inline-agent](plugins/inline-agent/planning.md)
602	- IxP model not yet trained -> use `core.logic.mock` and surface in Open Questions
603	
604	### "The flow needs something outside flow capabilities"
605	
606	1. Add a `core.logic.mock` placeholder
607	2. Note what needs to be created and which skill handles it:
608	   - Desktop/browser automation or coded workflow (C#) -> `uipath-rpa`
609	   - Agent -> `uipath-agents`
610	3. Phase 2 will check whether the resource has been published and replace the mock
611

It contains three sections: 38 39 ```json 40 { 41 "variables": { 42 "globals": [], 43 "nodes": [], 44 "variableUpdates": {} 45 } 46 } 47 ``` 48 49 | Section | Purpose | 50 | --- | --- | 51 | `globals` | Workflow-level variables: inputs, outputs, and state | 52 | `nodes` | Node output variables (auto-generated when using CLI `node add`) | 53 | `variableUpdates` | Per-node expressions that update state variables | 54 55 --- 56 57 ## Workflow Variables (`globals`) 58 59 Workflow variables are declared in `variables.globals`. Each has a **direction** that determines its role. 60 61 ### Directions 62 63 | Direction | Role | Readable | Writable | Use case | 64 | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | 65 | `in` | External input | Yes | No | Values passed when the flow is triggered or called | 66 | `out` | Workflow output | Yes | Mapped on End node | Values returned when the flow completes | 67 | `inout` | Internal state | Yes | Yes (via `variableUpdates`) | Counters, accumulators, flags shared across nodes | 68 69 ### Schema 70 71 ```typescript 72 { 73 id: string // Unique identifier, used in expressions as $vars.{id} 74 direction: "in" | "out" | "inout" 75 type?: string // "string" (default), "number", "boolean", "object", "array", "file" 76 subType?: string // Item type for arrays (e.g., "object", "string") 77 schema?: object // JSON Schema (draft-07) for complex types 78 defaultValue?: unknown // Initial value (must match type) 79 description?: string // Human-readable description 80 triggerNodeId?: string // Trigger node this input is associated with (works in both root flows and subflows) 81 } 82 ``` 83 84 ### Examples 85 86 **String input with default:** 87 ```json 88 { 89 "id": "customerName", 90 "direction": "in", 91 "type": "string", 92 "defaultValue": "Unknown", 93 "description": "Name of the customer to process" 94 } 95 ``` 96 97 **Number output:** 98 ```json 99 { 100 "id": "totalAmount", 101 "direction": "out", 102 "type": "number" 103 } 104 ``` 105 106 **State variable (counter):** 107 ```json 108 { 109 "id": "retryCount", 110 "direction": "inout", 111 "type": "number", 112 "defaultValue": 0 113 } 114 ``` 115 116 **Object with JSON Schema:** 117 ```json 118 { 119 "id": "orderData", 120 "direction": "in", 121 "type": "object", 122 "schema": { 123 "$schema": "http://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema#", 124 "type": "object", 125 "required": ["orderId", "amount"], 126 "properties": { 127 "orderId": { "type": "string" }, 128 "amount": { "type": "number" }, 129 "items": { 130 "type": "array", 131 "items": { "type": "object" } 132 } 133 }, 134 "additionalProperties": false 135 } 136 } 137 ``` 138 139 **Array with subType:** 140 ```json 141 { 142 "id": "emailList", 143 "direction": "in", 144 "type": "array", 145 "subType": "string", 146 "defaultValue": ["admin@example.com"] 147 } 148 ``` 149 150 **Input associated with a trigger:** 151 ```json 152 { 153 "id": "webhookPayload", 154 "direction": "in", 155 "type": "object", 156 "triggerNodeId": "start" 157 } 158 ``` 159 Accessed in expressions as `$vars.{triggerNodeId}.output.{id}` (the variable is nested under the trigger node's output — NOT `$vars.{id}`). 160 161 162 **File input (`type: "file"`):** 163 ```json 164 { 165 "id": "inputDoc", 166 "direction": "in", 167 "type": "file", 168 "description": "Document uploaded at trigger / bound via --attachment", 169 "triggerNodeId": "start" 170 } 171 ``` 172 173 > **Runtime shape of a `file` variable.** At runtime a `file` variable is an **object** (the *Flow Attachment* object), not a string. A Script node reading `$vars.start.output.inputDoc` receives: 174 > 175 > ```json 176 > { "ID": "", "FullName": "report.pdf", "MimeType": "application/pdf", "Metadata": { "size": "1024" } } 177 > ``` 178 > 179 > The uploaded file's name is **`.FullName`**. Property access is **case-sensitive** at runtime — these exact casings resolve, others return `undefined`/`null`: `.ID` (uppercase, not `.Id`), `.FullName`, `.MimeType`, and the **nested `.Metadata.size`** (lowercase `size`, NOT `.Size`). `.name` / `.fileName` do **not** exist. Two layers: the `.flow` *declaration* is camelCase (`type`, `direction`); the *runtime* object carries the casing above. Do NOT write `"FullName"` into the `.flow` source. Bind the file with `uip maestro flow debug --attachment =` — see [cli-commands.md — Pre-flight](cli-commands.md#attachment-preflight). 180 181 ### Type Reference 182 183 | Type | Default Value | Notes | 184 | --- | --- | --- | 185 | `string` | `""` | Default type if omitted | 186 | `number` | `0` | Integer or float | 187 | `boolean` | `false` | | 188 | `object` | `{}` | Use `schema` for structured objects | 189 | `array` | `[]` | Use `subType` for typed arrays | 190 | `file` | — | Bound at runtime via `--attachment`; hydrates as an object — read `.FullName` (see [File input](#file-input) above) | 191 192 --- 193 194 ## Node Variables (`nodes`) 195 196 Node variables represent outputs produced by nodes during execution. They are read-only and referenced via `$vars.{nodeId}.{outputId}`. 197 198 When you add a node via `uip maestro flow node add`, node variables are created automatically. When using `Edit` against the `.flow` file, add them manually. 199 200 ### Schema 201 202 ```typescript 203 { 204 id: string // Format: "{nodeId}.{outputId}" 205 type?: string // Output type 206 subType?: string // For complex types 207 schema?: object // JSON Schema for structured outputs 208 description?: string // What this output contains 209 binding: { 210 nodeId: string // Source node ID 211 outputId: string // Output port ID (e.g., "output", "error") 212 } 213 } 214 ``` 215 216 ### Example 217 218 ```json 219 { 220 "variables": { 221 "nodes": [ 222 { 223 "id": "fetchData.output", 224 "type": "object", 225 "description": "HTTP response body", 226 "binding": { 227 "nodeId": "fetchData", 228 "outputId": "output" 229 } 230 }, 231 { 232 "id": "fetchData.error", 233 "type": "object", 234 "description": "Error details if the request fails", 235 "schema": { 236 "$schema": "http://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema#", 237 "type": "object", 238 "required": ["code", "message"], 239 "properties": { 240 "code": { "type": "string" }, 241 "message": { "type": "string" }, 242 "detail": { "type": "string" }, 243 "category": { "type": "string" }, 244 "status": { "type": "integer" } 245 } 246 }, 247 "binding": { 248 "nodeId": "fetchData", 249 "outputId": "error" 250 } 251 } 252 ] 253 } 254 } 255 ``` 256 257 --- 258 259 ## Variable Updates (`variableUpdates`) 260 261 Variable updates assign new values to `inout` (state) variables at specific nodes. They execute when the node completes. 262 263 ### Schema 264 265 ```typescript 266 { 267 "variableUpdates": { 268 "{nodeId}": [ 269 { 270 "variableId": string, // ID of the inout variable to update 271 "expression": string // =js: expression to evaluate and assign 272 } 273 ] 274 } 275 } 276 ``` 277 278 ### Example 279 280 ```json 281 { 282 "variables": { 283 "globals": [ 284 { 285 "id": "counter", 286 "direction": "inout", 287 "type": "number", 288 "defaultValue": 0 289 }, 290 { 291 "id": "lastStatus", 292 "direction": "inout", 293 "type": "string", 294 "defaultValue": "pending" 295 } 296 ], 297 "variableUpdates": { 298 "processItem": [ 299 { 300 "variableId": "counter", 301 "expression": "=js:$vars.counter + 1" 302 }, 303 { 304 "variableId": "lastStatus", 305 "expression": "=js:$vars.processItem.output.status" 306 } 307 ] 308 } 309 } 310 } 311 ``` 312 313 > **Only `inout` variables can be updated.** Updating an `in` or `out` variable is invalid. 314 315 > **Inside loops:** variableUpdate expressions cannot access loop iteration variables like `$vars..currentItem`. Those are only available inside the body node's script. The variableUpdate must reference the body node's output (e.g., `=js:$vars.bodyNode.output`). 316 317 --- 318 319 ## Output Mapping on End Nodes 320 321 Workflow output variables (`direction: "out"`) must be mapped on End nodes. The End node's `outputs` object maps each output variable ID to a source expression. 322 323 ### Structure 324 325 ```json 326 { 327 "id": "end1", 328 "type": "core.control.end", 329 "typeVersion": "1.0", 330 "display": { "label": "End" }, 331 "inputs": {}, 332 "outputs": { 333 "totalAmount": { 334 "source": "=js:$vars.calculateTotal.output.amount" 335 }, 336 "summary": { 337 "source": "=js:$vars.formatResult.output.text" 338 } 339 } 340 } 341 ``` 342 343 > **Every `out` variable must have a mapping on every End node** that the flow can reach. Missing mappings cause runtime errors. 344 345 --- 346 347 ## Expression System 348 349 Flow uses a **Jint-based JavaScript engine** (ES2020 subset) for expressions. There are two expression formats. 350 351 ### `=js:` Expressions (Full JavaScript) 352 353 Used for conditions, input values, variable updates, and output mappings. The `=js:` prefix tells the engine to evaluate the rest as JavaScript. 354 355 ``` 356 =js:$vars.order.amount > 1000 && $vars.order.status === "approved" 357 ``` 358 359 ### Template Expressions (`{ }`) 360 361 Used for string interpolation in **native flow string fields** only. Expressions inside single braces are evaluated and converted to strings. 362 363 ``` 364 Order {$vars.orderId} is {$vars.status} — total: {$vars.amount} 365 ``` 366 367 > **Brace-templates do NOT work in Integration Service activity inputs.** The flow-layer template runner only processes native flow fields (decision expressions, variable updates, end-node output `source`, script bodies, agent prompt text). Fields inside `inputs.detail.bodyParameters` on `core.action.http.v2` or `uipath.connector.*` activity nodes — `url`, `headers`, `body`, `query` — are passed through to the IS runtime unchanged, so `{$vars.article}` ships literally. Observed behavior: the `$` is stripped and the braces survive (`user/{vars.article}` reaches the service). **For any dynamic value in an IS activity input, use `=js:` instead** — e.g., `` "url": "=js:`https://.../user/${$vars.article}`" `` or `"headers": { "Authorization": "=js:'Bearer ' + $vars.token" }`. 368 369 ### IS Activity Inputs Require `=js:` (Critical) 370 371 Every `$vars` / `$metadata` / `$self` reference inside `inputs.detail.bodyParameters`, `inputs.detail.queryParameters`, or `inputs.detail.pathParameters` on a connector or HTTP activity node MUST be wrapped with `=js:`. Without it the value ships as a literal string at runtime. 372 373 | Wrong | Right | 374 |---|---| 375 | `"recordId": "$vars.createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | `"recordId": "=js:$vars.createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | 376 | `"recordId": "nodes.createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | `"recordId": "=js:$vars.createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | 377 | `"recordId": "{vars.createEntityRecord1.output.Id}"` | `"recordId": "=js:$vars.createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | 378 | `"recordId": "=js:createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | `"recordId": "=js:$vars.createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | 379 380 The serializer rewrites `$vars` → `vars` whether or not `=js:` is present, so a missing prefix yields a confusing failure: the runtime field is bound to the literal string `"vars.X.output.Id"` (which looks like an unevaluated expression). The last row above is the opposite mistake — `=js:` is present but the `$vars.` prefix on the node reference is missing, so the expression evaluates a bare (undefined) identifier instead of the node's output. `flow validate` catches this (cli-side `expression-prefix-validator`, error with remediation hint) — older cli versions without the validator still let it through to `flow debug`. See [node-output-wiring.md](node-output-wiring.md) for the full per-node-type field reference (MST-9107). 381 382 ### Comparison 383 384 | Feature | `=js:` | `{ }` template | 385 | --- | --- | --- | 386 | Return type | Any (boolean, number, object, array) | Always string | 387 | Use case | Conditions, inputs, mappings | Native flow text/prompt fields only | 388 | Works in IS activity inputs (HTTP URL/headers/body, connector `bodyParameters`) | Yes | **No — use `=js:`** | 389 | Full JS | Yes | Expression-only (no statements) | 390 | Prefix | `=js:` required | No prefix, braces inline | 391 392 --- 393 394 ## Available Globals 395 396 These variables are available in all expression contexts: 397 398 | Global | Description | Access pattern | 399 | --- | --- | --- | 400 | `$vars` | All workflow and node variables | `$vars.{variableId}` or `$vars.{nodeId}.{outputId}` | 401 | `$metadata` | Workflow metadata (instanceId, executionId) | `$metadata.instanceId` | 402 | `$self` | Current node's output (HTTP branch conditions only) | `$self.output.statusCode` | 403 | `$vars..*` | Loop iteration context (inside loops only) | `$vars.loop1.currentItem`, `$vars.loop1.currentIndex` | 404 405 ### `$vars` Access Patterns 406 407 ```javascript 408 // Workflow global 409 $vars.customerName 410 $vars.counter 411 412 // Trigger-associated flow input (triggerNodeId set) 413 $vars.{triggerNodeId}.output.{id} 414 415 // File input (type: "file") → object, read .FullName for the name 416 $vars.start.output.inputDoc.FullName 417 418 // Node output (script node) 419 $vars.script1.output 420 $vars.script1.output.someField 421 422 // Node output (HTTP node) 423 $vars.fetchData.output.body 424 $vars.fetchData.output.statusCode 425 $vars.fetchData.output.headers 426 427 // Node error 428 $vars.fetchData.error.message 429 $vars.fetchData.error.code 430 ``` 431 432 --- 433 434 ## Expression Contexts 435 436 Expressions behave differently depending on where they appear. 437 438 ### Script Node Body 439 440 The `inputs.script` field contains a function body. Full JavaScript statements are allowed (variables, loops, conditionals). The returned value becomes `$vars.{nodeId}.output`. 441 442 Scripts can return any value — objects, numbers, strings, arrays, or booleans: 443 444 ```javascript 445 // Returning an object (multiple fields) 446 const items = $vars.fetchData.output.body.items; 447 const filtered = items.filter(i => i.active); 448 return { count: filtered.length, names: filtered.map(i => i.name) }; 449 450 // Returning a bare value (useful for accumulators in loops) 451 return $vars.total + $vars.loop1.currentItem; 452 ``` 453 454 ### Decision Node (`inputs.expression`) 455 456 A single boolean expression. Result is coerced to `Boolean()`. 457 458 ``` 459 =js:$vars.order.amount > 1000 && $vars.order.verified === true 460 ``` 461 462 Determines which port fires: `true` or `false`. 463 464 ### Switch Node (`inputs.cases[].expression`) 465 466 Each case has an expression evaluated in order. First truthy result wins; otherwise the `default` port fires. 467 468 ```json 469 { 470 "inputs": { 471 "cases": [ 472 { "label": "Low", "expression": "$vars.score <= 30" }, 473 { "label": "Medium", "expression": "$vars.score <= 70" }, 474 { "label": "High", "expression": "$vars.score > 70" } 475 ] 476 } 477 } 478 ``` 479 480 ### HTTP Branch Condition (`inputs.branches[].conditionExpression`) 481 482 Uses `$self` to reference the current HTTP node's response. 483 484 ``` 485 $self.output.statusCode >= 200 && $self.output.statusCode < 300 486 ``` 487 488 ### Variable Update Expressions 489 490 Evaluate to the new value for the target variable. 491 492 ``` 493 =js:$vars.counter + 1 494 =js:$vars.items.concat([$vars.newItem.output]) 495 ``` 496 497 ### Loop Collection Expression 498 499 The `inputs.collection` field on a Loop node resolves to an array to iterate over. 500 501 ``` 502 =js:$vars.fetchData.output.body.items 503 =js:$vars.inputArray.filter(x => x.active) 504 ``` 505 506 Inside the loop body, use `$vars..currentItem` and `$vars..currentIndex` (e.g., `$vars.loop1.currentItem`). 507 508 --- 509 510 ## Jint Engine Constraints 511 512 The production runtime uses **Jint** (a .NET JavaScript interpreter, ES2020 subset). Key constraints: 513 514 ### Supported 515 516 - Arithmetic: `+`, `-`, `*`, `/`, `%` 517 - Comparison: `===`, `!==`, `==`, `!=`, `>`, `<`, `>=`, `<=` 518 - Logical: `&&`, `||`, `!` 519 - Ternary: `condition ? a : b` 520 - String methods: `.toUpperCase()`, `.toLowerCase()`, `.trim()`, `.split()`, `.includes()`, `.startsWith()`, `.slice()`, `.substring()` 521 - Array methods: `.filter()`, `.map()`, `.reduce()`, `.find()`, `.some()`, `.every()`, `.concat()`, `.length` 522 - Object: `Object.keys()`, `Object.values()`, `Object.entries()` 523 - Math: `Math.floor()`, `Math.ceil()`, `Math.round()`, `Math.abs()`, `Math.min()`, `Math.max()`, `Math.random()` 524 - JSON: `JSON.parse()`, `JSON.stringify()` 525 - Template literals: `` `Hello ${name}` `` 526 - Destructuring: `const { a, b } = obj` (in script bodies) 527 - Spread operator: `[...arr1, ...arr2]` (in script bodies) 528 - Arrow functions: `items.filter(x => x.active)` (inline callbacks) 529 530 ### Not Supported 531 532 - `fetch`, `XMLHttpRequest`, `setTimeout`, `setInterval` — no network or timers 533 - `document`, `window`, `console` — no DOM or browser globals 534 - `require`, `import` — no module system 535 - `eval`, `Function` constructor — no dynamic code generation 536 - `async`/`await`, `Promise` — no async operations 537 - `Date` constructor may have limited support — prefer ISO 8601 strings 538 539 > **When in doubt, keep expressions simple.** Complex data processing should go in Script nodes where you have full statement support, not in one-line expressions. 540 541 --- 542 543 ## Scoping Rules 544 545 ### Node Output Availability 546 547 A node's output (`$vars.{nodeId}.output`) is available to **all downstream nodes** connected via edges. If a node has not executed (e.g., on an untaken branch), its `$vars` entry is `undefined`. 548 549 ### Loop Scope 550 551 Inside a loop body, you have access to: 552 - All parent-scope `$vars` (read-only from loop's perspective) 553 - `$vars..currentItem` — current array element 554 - `$vars..currentIndex` — zero-based index 555 - `$vars..collection` — the original array 556 557 Where `` is the loop node's `id` (e.g., `$vars.loop1.currentItem`). 558 559 > **Important:** Loop body nodes must have `"parentId": ""` set in their JSON. Without this, the runtime does not know the node is inside the loop and `$vars..currentItem` will be undefined. 560 561 After loop completion, `$vars..output` contains aggregated results from all iterations. 562 563 ### Subflow Scope 564 565 Subflows have their own variable scope. Parent variables are **not** automatically visible inside a subflow. Pass values explicitly via subflow `inputs` and receive results via subflow `outputs`. 566 567 --- 568 569 ## Variable Management via CLI 570 571 There are **no CLI commands** for adding or removing variables. Manage variables with `Edit` against the `.flow` file. 572 573 ### Adding a workflow input variable 574 575 1. Open `.flow` 576 2. Add the variable object to `variables.globals` 577 3. Run `uip maestro flow validate` to check for errors 578 579 ### Adding node variables after manual node insertion 580 581 When adding nodes via `Edit` (not CLI), you must also add corresponding entries to `variables.nodes`: 582 583 ```json 584 { 585 "id": "myScript.output", 586 "type": "object", 587 "binding": { "nodeId": "myScript", "outputId": "output" } 588 }, 589 { 590 "id": "myScript.error", 591 "type": "object", 592 "binding": { "nodeId": "myScript", "outputId": "error" } 593 } 594 ``` 595 596 > **When using `uip maestro flow node add`**, node variables are handled automatically. Only add them manually when using `Edit` against the `.flow` file. 597 598 ### Mapping outputs on End nodes 599 600 For every `out` variable, add a mapping in each End node's `outputs`: 601 602 ```json 603 "outputs": { 604 "result": { 605 "source": "=js:$vars.processData.output" 606 } 607 } 608 ``` 609 610 --- 611 612 ## Complete Example 613 614 A flow with input, state, and output "description": "Items to process" 627 }, 628 { 629 "id": "processedCount", 630 "direction": "inout", 631 "type": "number", 632 "defaultValue": 0 633 }, 634 { 635 "id": "result", 636 "direction": 1	# HTTP Request Node — Implementation
2	
3	This page is the entry point for implementing a managed HTTP node. Pick your auth mode below, then follow the matching walkthrough end-to-end. The "Shared Reference" section is an appendix — the mode walkthroughs already inline what you need to act, and link here only for full rationale and extended examples.
4	
5	## Node Type
6	
7	`core.action.http.v2` (Managed HTTP Request)
8	
9	> **Always use `core.action.http.v2`** for all HTTP requests. The older `core.action.http` (v1) is deprecated.
10	
11	## Pick a Mode
12	
13	| Mode | Use when | Walkthrough |
14	| --- | --- | --- |
15	| **Connector** | Target system has an IS connector — auth via an existing IS connection (OAuth/API key) | [impl-connector.md](impl-connector.md) |
16	| **Manual** | No connector exists, public/no-auth API, or quick prototyping | [impl-manual.md](impl-manual.md) |
17	
18	> **Mode fallback — auto-try, then confirm.** Prefer a curated connector activity first; if none, use connector mode; if connector mode cannot be configured (connector lacks HTTP request support — `HasHttpRequest` false — or no usable IS connection), fall through to manual mode automatically. Manual changes the auth model (you supply auth yourself), so confirm the switched mode with the user before finalizing. See [impl-connector.md — Step 2](impl-connector.md#step-2--identify-target-connection).
19	
20	The `--detail` payload differs in two places between modes: `authentication` (`"connector"` vs `"manual"`), and the connector-binding fields `targetConnector` / `connectionId` / `folderKey` (connector mode only; `url` is then relative to the connector base, vs. an absolute URL in manual mode). Everything else (node add, dynamic values, branches, edges, debug) is shared.
21	
22	## Critical: Use `node configure`
23	
24	> **Do not hand-write `inputs.detail`, `bindings_v2.json`, or connection resource files.** Run `uip maestro flow node configure` — it builds everything from a simple `--detail` JSON. Hand-written configurations miss the `essentialConfiguration` block and fail at runtime. `core.action.http.v2` is CLI-owned per [Author capability — Node ownership](../../../CAPABILITY.md#node-ownership--who-authors-the-node) (same envelope rules as connector activities).
25	
26	## Registry validation
27	
28	```bash
29	uip maestro flow registry get core.action.http.v2 --output json
30	```
31	
32	Confirm in `Data.Node.handleConfiguration`: target port `input`, source ports `branch-{item.id}` (dynamic, `repeat: inputs.branches`) and `default`. Also confirm `Data.Node.supportsErrorHandling: true` — HTTP v2 participates in the implicit `error` port pattern shared by every action node (see [Action Node Structure](../../../../shared/action-nodes.md)). Model `serviceType` is `Intsvc.UnifiedHttpRequest`.

36	## Shared Reference (appendix)
37	
38	The mode walkthroughs link into the sections below for full rationale and extended examples. You do not need to read this section in order — jump directly from the walkthrough link that brought you here.
39	
40	### Add the node
41	
42	```bash
43	uip maestro flow node add <ProjectName>.flow core.action.http.v2 \
44	  --label "<HTTP node label>" --output json
45	```
46	
47	The CLI copies the manifest into `definitions[]`, adds the node instance to `nodes[]`, registers the `variables.nodes` entries, and inserts a placeholder in `layout.nodes` — all in code, byte-for-byte from the registry (including `typeVersion`, which the CLI pulls from the manifest's `version` field; do not hardcode it). Save the returned node ID — both walkthroughs reuse it.
48	
49	The CLI initializes `inputs` from the manifest's `inputDefaults`:
50	
51	```json
52	"inputs": {
53	  "branches": [],
54	  "timeout": "PT15M",
55	  "retryCount": 0,
56	  "swaggerDefinition": null,
57	  "detail": {}
58	}
59	```
60	
61	`inputs.detail` is populated by the configure step (next). The inputs-level siblings — `branches`, `timeout`, `retryCount` — are set at `node add` time via `--input`:
62	
63	```bash
64	uip maestro flow node add <ProjectName>.flow core.action.http.v2 \
65	  --label "<HTTP node label>" \
66	  --input '{
67	    "timeout": "PT30M",
68	    "retryCount": 3,
69	    "branches": [
70	      { "id": "hasItems", "name": "Has Items", "conditionExpression": "$self.output.body.items.length > 0" },
71	      { "id": "empty",    "name": "Empty",    "conditionExpression": "$self.output.body.items.length == 0" }
72	    ]
73	  }' --output json
74	```
75	
76	- `timeout` — ISO 8601 duration (e.g. `PT15M`, `PT1H`, `P1D`). Default `PT15M`.
77	- `retryCount` — integer. Default `0`.
78	- `branches` — see [Conditional branches](#conditional-branches) below.
79	
80	> **Do not hand-author the `core.action.http.v2` definition, and do not `Edit` `inputs.*` after the fact.** Use `uip maestro flow node add` (with `--input` for branches/timeout/retryCount) and `uip maestro flow node configure` (for `inputs.detail`). These are the only supported authoring paths.
81	
82	### Dynamic values in URL / headers / body / query
83	
84	**IS activity input fields do not resolve `{$vars.x}` brace-templates.** The flow runtime's `{...}` template interpolation only applies to native flow fields (end-node output `source`, variable updates, decision `expression`, script body, etc.) — **not** to fields under `inputs.detail.bodyParameters` on HTTP v2 or on any `uipath.connector.*` activity. Evidence: `"url": "https://.../user/{$vars.article}/..."` ships to the service as literal `{vars.article}` (the `$` is stripped, braces remain), producing a 400 Bad Request.
85	
86	**Use `=js:` expressions for any dynamic value in IS activity inputs.** The runtime evaluates `=js:` before handing the value to the connector:
87	
88	```json
89	"bodyParameters": {
90	  "url": "=js:`https://api.example.com/users/${$vars.userId}/orders`",
91	  "headers": {
92	    "Authorization": "=js:'Bearer ' + $vars.apiToken",
93	    "X-Request-ID": "=js:$metadata.instanceId"
94	  },
95	  "query": {
96	    "since": "=js:$vars.startDate"
97	  }
98	}
99	```
100	
101	Template literals with `${...}` interpolation work because the whole expression is evaluated as JavaScript — `$vars` is a global in the `=js:` context. Plain string concatenation (`'Bearer ' + $vars.token`) works the same way.
102	
103	When calling `uip maestro flow node configure --detail`, pass the `=js:` string verbatim — the CLI stores it in `inputs.detail.bodyParameters` unchanged:
104	
105	```bash
106	uip maestro flow node configure <Project>.flow <nodeId> \
107	  --detail '{
108	    "authentication": "manual",
109	    "method": "GET",
110	    "url": "=js:`https://api.example.com/users/${$vars.userId}`"
111	  }' --output json
112	```
113	
114	### Conditional branches
115	
116	Skip this section unless you need to route downstream paths based on the *response content* (e.g., `items.length > 0` vs empty). Do **not** use `branches` just to handle call failures — for that, use the `error` port (see [Wire edges](#wire-edges)).
117	
118	Each branch entry creates a `branch-{id}` source port. `$self` refers to the current HTTP node's output inside the condition.
119	
120	Set `branches` at `node add` time via `--input` (see [Add the node](#add-the-node)) — `branches` lives at `inputs.branches`, not `inputs.detail.branches`, and `node configure --detail` does not accept it.
121	
122	```bash
123	uip maestro flow node add <ProjectName>.flow core.action.http.v2 \
124	  --label "<HTTP node label>" \
125	  --input '{
126	    "branches": [
127	      { "id": "hasItems", "name": "Has Items", "conditionExpression": "$self.output.body.items.length > 0" },
128	      { "id": "empty",    "name": "Empty",    "conditionExpression": "$self.output.body.items.length == 0" }
129	    ]
130	  }' --output json
131	```
132	
133	> **Do not prefix `conditionExpression` with `=js:`** — HTTP branch conditions are auto-evaluated as JS (same rule as decision/switch expressions).
134	
135	### Wire edges
136	
137	The managed HTTP node's target port is `input`. Its source ports are:
138	
139	- `default` — primary success output (or fallback when configured branches don't match)
140	- `error` — fires when the HTTP call fails (network error, timeout, non-2xx not caught by a branch); wire this to an error handler to keep the flow from faulting
141	- `branch-{id}` — one per entry in `inputs.branches` ([Conditional branches](#conditional-branches)); use the exact `id` you set
142	
143	Use `Edit` to add edge objects to `edges[]`; do not use `uip maestro flow edge add` for this structural wiring. Examples:
144	
145	```json
146	{
147	  "id": "e-<upstreamNodeId>-<nodeId>",
148	  "sourceNodeId": "<upstreamNodeId>",
149	  "sourcePort": "<port>",
150	  "targetNodeId": "<nodeId>",
151	  "targetPort": "input"
152	}
153	```
154	
155	```json
156	{
157	  "id": "e-<nodeId>-<downstreamNodeId>",
158	  "sourceNodeId": "<nodeId>",
159	  "sourcePort": "default",
160	  "targetNodeId": "<downstreamNodeId>",
161	  "targetPort": "input"
162	}
163	```
164	
165	```json
166	{
167	  "id": "e-<nodeId>-<errorHandlerId>",
168	  "sourceNodeId": "<nodeId>",
169	  "sourcePort": "error",
170	  "targetNodeId": "<errorHandlerId>",
171	  "targetPort": "input"
172	}
173	```
174	
175	When an HTTP node has an outgoing `error` edge, the HTTP node instance must also include `inputs.errorHandlingEnabled: true`. `uip maestro flow edge add --source-port error` and `uip maestro flow format` set this automatically; direct JSON edits must set it explicitly.
176	
177	```json
178	{
179	  "id": "e-<nodeId>-<hasItemsDownstream>",
180	  "sourceNodeId": "<nodeId>",
181	  "sourcePort": "branch-hasItems",
182	  "targetNodeId": "<hasItemsDownstream>",
183	  "targetPort": "input"
184	}
185	```
186	
187	### Debug
188	
189	| Error | Cause | Fix |
190	| --- | --- | --- |
191	| `not_authed` or 401/403 | Wrong node type (v1 instead of v2), missing bindings, or expired connection | Verify node type is `core.action.http.v2`, check `bindings_v2.json` exists, ping the connection |
192	| `configuration` field missing | Node not configured via CLI | Run `uip maestro flow node configure` — do not hand-write `inputs.detail` |
193	| `flow validate` errors with `uiPathActivityTypeId` missing on `core.action.http.v2` | Node was hand-authored in `definitions[]` instead of via `uip maestro flow node add` | Remove the node, re-add it via `uip maestro flow node add <file> core.action.http.v2 ...`, then re-run `node configure`. |
194	| Connection not found | Wrong connection ID or connector key | Re-run `uip is connections list` for the target connector |
195	| Wrong API response | Incorrect `url` or `query` | Check the target service's API documentation |
196	| `ImplicitConnection` errors | Manual mode misconfigured | Verify `authentication: "manual"` and `url` is a full URL |
197	| Flow faults on 4xx/5xx response | No `error` edge wired from the HTTP node | Add an edge with `sourcePort: "error"` to an error-handler node. See [Implicit error port on action nodes](../../../../shared/file-format.md#implicit-error-port-on-action-nodes) — same mechanism applies to all action nodes |
198	| Edge `source-port output` rejected | Referencing the variable namespace as a port name | HTTP source ports are `default`, `error`, and `branch-{id}` — not `output`. The `output` name is only a variable namespace (`$vars.{nodeId}.output`) |
199

1	# Script Node — Implementation
2	
3	## Node Type
4	
5	`core.action.script`
6	
7	## Registry validation
8	
9	```bash
10	uip maestro flow registry get core.action.script --output json
11	```
12	
13	Confirm: input port `input`, output port `success`, required input `script` (string, non-empty). See [Action Node Structure — Registry validation](../../../../shared/action-nodes.md#registry-validation) for the shared pattern.
14	
15	## JSON structure
16	
17	Follow the [Action Node Structure — Standard JSON skeleton](../../../../shared/action-nodes.md#standard-json-skeleton). The script-specific input is a single `script` string:
18	
19	```json
20	{
21	  "inputs": {
22	    "script": "const items = $vars.fetchData.output.body.items;\nconst total = items.reduce((sum, i) => sum + i.amount, 0);\nreturn { total, count: items.length };"
23	  }
24	}
25	```
26	
27	## Adding and editing
28	
29	See [Action Node Structure — Adding and editing procedures](../../../../shared/action-nodes.md#adding-and-editing-procedures). The script node uses the standard input port `input` and output port `success`; no plugin-specific wiring.
30	
31	## Script rules
32	
33	1. **Top-level body — no `function main()` wrapper.** Node runs the `script` text directly (as a function body); a wrapper is never called → `output` null. Read workflow variables via `$vars.<variableId>` and upstream node outputs via `$vars.<nodeId>.output`; end with top-level `return {…}`. Not a coded Function: no `main`, no injected args.
34	   - Correct: `const n = $vars.ixp1.output.field; return { n };`
35	   - Wrong: `function main({ ixp1 }) { … }`
36	2. **Must `return` an object** — `return { key: value }`, not a bare scalar. The return value becomes `$vars.<nodeId>.output`.
37	3. **`$vars` is a global** — use it directly: `return { upper: $vars.customerName.toUpperCase() }`
38	4. **JavaScript ES2020 (Jint engine)** — see [variables-and-expressions.md](../../../../shared/variables-and-expressions.md) for supported features and Jint constraints.
39	5. **No `console.log`** — `console` is not available. Use `return { debug: value }` to inspect values.
40	6. **No external calls** — use the HTTP node or a connector node for API calls.
41	7. **30-second timeout** — long-running computations will be killed.
42	
43	## Common patterns
44	
45	### Transform and return
46	
47	```javascript
48	const items = $vars.fetchData.output.body.items;
49	const filtered = items.filter(i => i.status === "active");
50	return { items: filtered, count: filtered.length };
51	```
52	
53	### Build a payload for a downstream node
54	
55	```javascript
56	return {
57	  subject: `Order ${$vars.orderId} - Confirmation`,
58	  body: `Your order of ${$vars.orderTotal} has been processed.`,
59	  recipient: $vars.customerEmail
60	};
61	```
62	
63	### Error check from upstream
64	
65	```javascript
66	const error = $vars.httpCall.error;
67	if (error) {
68	  return { hasError: true, message: error.message };
69	}
70	return { hasError: false, data: $vars.httpCall.output.body };
71	```
72	
73	### Reading a file-typed variable
74	
75	A `file` variable (bound via `uip maestro flow debug --attachment <id>=<path>`) hydrates as an **object**, not a string. Read the uploaded file's name from `.FullName`:
76	
77	```javascript
78	const doc = $vars.start.output.inputDoc; // file variable → object
79	return { fileName: doc.FullName };        // .FullName, not .name/.fileName
80	```
81	
82	Property access is **case-sensitive** — these casings resolve: `.FullName`, `.ID` (uppercase, not `.Id`), `.MimeType`, `.Metadata.size` (nested, lowercase `size`). `.name` / `.fileName` do not exist. See [variables-and-expressions.md — Runtime shape of a `file` variable](../../../../shared/variables-and-expressions.md#file-input).
83	
84	## Debug
85	
86	| Error | Cause | Fix |
87	| --- | --- | --- |
88	| Script did not return a value | Missing `return` statement | Add `return { ... }` |
89	| `output` is `null` but script has a `return` | `return` is inside an uncalled `function main(){}` wrapper | Remove wrapper; code + `return` at top level (rule 1) |
90	| Return value is not an object | Returned a scalar (`return 42`) | Wrap in object: `return { value: 42 }` |
91	| `$vars.nodeId` is undefined | Upstream node not connected or wrong ID | Check edges and node IDs |
92	| Timeout after 30s | Script too expensive | Simplify logic or split into multiple scripts |
93	| `console is not defined` | Used `console.log()` | Remove — use `return { debug: val }` instead |
94	| `fetch is not defined` | Tried to make HTTP call | Use an HTTP node or connector node instead |
95

1	# HTTP Request Node — Manual Mode
2	
3	Use this walkthrough when there is no IS connector for the target service, the API needs no auth (or auth you pass yourself in headers), or you are prototyping against an arbitrary REST endpoint. For connector-managed auth, use [impl-connector.md](impl-connector.md) instead.
4	
5	**No connection lookup required.** Manual mode uses `ImplicitConnection` — there are no IS bindings.
6	
7	Before starting, read [impl.md](impl.md) for the node type, registry validation, and the "always use `node configure`" rule. Follow Steps 1–4 in order.
8	
9	## Step 1 — Add the node
10	
11	```bash
12	uip maestro flow node add <ProjectName>.flow core.action.http.v2 \
13	  --label "<HTTP node label>" --output json
14	```
15	
16	The CLI copies the manifest into `definitions[]`, adds the node instance, registers `variables.nodes`, and inserts a `layout.nodes` placeholder — byte-for-byte from the registry. Save the returned `<nodeId>` — Step 2 reuses it. Leave `inputs` empty; Step 2 populates `inputs.detail`. Do not hand-author the definition — see [impl.md — Add the node](impl.md#add-the-node).
17	
18	## Step 2 — Configure the node
19	
20	> **Find missing values first.** Before composing `url` / `query` / `body`, resolve any values the agent doesn't have (IDs from names, required body fields, response shape, …). See [/uipath:uipath-platform — http-request.md](../../../../../../uipath-platform/references/integration-service/http-request.md).
21	
22	```bash
23	uip maestro flow node configure <ProjectName>.flow <nodeId> \
24	  --detail '{
25	    "authentication": "manual",
26	    "method": "GET",
27	    "url": "https://api.example.com/endpoint",
28	    "query": {"param1": "value1"}
29	  }' --output json
30	```
31	
32	The CLI:
33	
34	- Builds the full `inputs.detail` (manual auth, `ImplicitConnection`, bodyParameters, essentialConfiguration)
35	- Does **not** generate `bindings_v2.json` or a connection resource file — manual mode needs neither
36	
37	`url` must be a full URL (scheme + host + path). For auth headers you control, pass them under `headers`:
38	
39	```bash
40	uip maestro flow node configure <ProjectName>.flow <nodeId> \
41	  --detail '{
42	    "authentication": "manual",
43	    "method": "GET",
44	    "url": "https://api.example.com/me",
45	    "headers": {"Authorization": "=js:`Bearer ${$vars.apiToken}`"}
46	  }' --output json
47	```
48	
49	**Dynamic values:** HTTP input fields do not resolve `{$vars.x}` brace-templates — use `=js:` expressions for any dynamic `url` / `headers` / `body` / `query`. Pass the `=js:` string verbatim in `--detail`. Full rationale and examples: [impl.md — Dynamic values](impl.md#dynamic-values-in-url--headers--body--query).
50	
51	## Step 3 — (Optional) Response branches
52	
53	Skip unless you need to route downstream paths based on response content (e.g., `items.length > 0` vs empty). For generic call-failure handling use the `error` port in Step 4 instead. Full syntax and rules: [impl.md — Conditional branches](impl.md#conditional-branches).
54	
55	## Step 4 — Wire edges
56	
57	The HTTP node's target port is `input`. Source ports: `default` (success), `error` (network/non-2xx), `branch-{id}` (one per Step 3 entry). Wire `default` to the next node and `error` to a handler — without an `error` edge, a failed call faults the flow.
58	
59	Edge JSON shapes and all four examples (upstream→node, default→downstream, error→handler, branch→downstream): [impl.md — Wire edges](impl.md#wire-edges).
60	
61	## Debug
62	
63	See [impl.md — Debug](impl.md#debug). For manual mode, watch for `ImplicitConnection` errors — they signal a missing `authentication: "manual"` flag or a non-URL `url` value.
64

1	# End Node — Implementation
2	
3	## Node Type
4	
5	`core.control.end`
6	
7	## Registry Validation
8	
9	```bash
10	uip maestro flow registry get core.control.end --output json
11	```
12	
13	Confirm: input port `input`, no output ports. Set the node instance `typeVersion` to the `version` field from this response — do not hardcode it.
14	
15	## JSON Structure
16	
17	### Without Output Mapping
18	
19	```json
20	{
21	  "id": "doneSuccess",
22	  "type": "core.control.end",
23	  "typeVersion": "<DEFINITION_VERSION>",
24	  "display": { "label": "Done" },
25	  "inputs": {}
26	}
27	```
28	
29	### With Output Mapping
30	
31	When the workflow declares `out` variables, every End node must map all of them:
32	
33	```json
34	{
35	  "id": "doneSuccess",
36	  "type": "core.control.end",
37	  "typeVersion": "<DEFINITION_VERSION>",
38	  "display": { "label": "Done" },
39	  "inputs": {},
40	  "outputs": {
41	    "processedCount": {
42	      "source": "=js:$vars.processData.output.count"
43	    },
44	    "resultSummary": {
45	      "source": "=js:$vars.formatOutput.output.summary"
46	    }
47	  }
48	}
49	```
50	
51	Each key in `outputs` must match a variable `id` from `variables.globals` where `direction: "out"`.
52	
53	## Adding / Editing
54	
55	For step-by-step add, delete, and wiring procedures, see [editing-operations.md](../../editing-operations.md). Use the JSON structure above for the node-specific `inputs` and `outputs`.
56	
57	Output mapping must be added with `Edit` against the `.flow` file — see [Edit/Write: Add output mapping](../../editing-operations-json.md#add-output-mapping-on-an-end-node).
58	
59	## Debug
60	
61	| Error | Cause | Fix |
62	| --- | --- | --- |
63	| Missing output mapping | `out` variable not mapped on this End node | Add `outputs.{varId}.source` expression for every `out` variable |
64	| Output expression unresolvable | `$vars` reference points to unreachable node | Ensure the node is upstream and connected via edges |
65	| Runtime silent failure | Output mapping missing on one reachable End node | Check **all** End nodes, not just the primary path |
66

1	# Action Node Structure
2	
3	Reference for the boilerplate shared by every action-node `impl.md` in this skill. Plugin docs should link here for the standard parts and only spell out what is plugin-specific: the registry type string, plugin-specific input fields, plugin-specific rules, debug entries, and node-type configuration workflows.
4	
5	## Registry validation
6	
7	Every action node should validate its registry contract before authoring:
8	
9	```bash
10	uip maestro flow registry get <node-type> --output json
11	```
12	
13	`registry get` returns the manifest at `Data.Node`. Do **not** inspect `Data` directly as if it were the node manifest.
14	
15	```json
16	{
17	  "Data": {
18	    "Node": {
19	      "nodeType": "core.action.script",
20	      "version": "1.0",
21	      "handleConfiguration": [
22	        { "position": "left", "handles": [{ "id": "input", "type": "target" }] },
23	        { "position": "right", "handles": [{ "id": "success", "type": "source" }] }
24	      ],
25	      "inputDefinition": {},
26	      "outputDefinition": {}
27	    }
28	  }
29	}
30	```
31	
32	Inspect:
33	
34	- `Data.Node.handleConfiguration` — input port name and output port name(s). Array of position groups, not a map with a top-level `handles` field.
35	- `Data.Node.inputDefinition` — required inputs.
36	- `Data.Node.outputDefinition` — downstream payloads.
37	- `Data.Node.model.serviceType` — where applicable.
38	
39	Plugin `impl.md` records what to confirm for that specific node type.
40	
41	## Standard JSON skeleton
42	
43	All action nodes share this base shape on the node instance:
44	
45	```json
46	{
47	  "id": "<nodeId>",
48	  "type": "<node-type>",
49	  "typeVersion": "<version>",
50	  "display": { "label": "<Label>" },
51	  "inputs": { /* plugin-specific — see plugin impl.md */ },
52	  "outputs": {
53	    "output": {
54	      "type": "object",
55	      "description": "<plugin-specific description>",
56	      "source": "=result.response",
57	      "var": "output"
58	    },
59	    "error": {
60	      "type": "object",
61	      "description": "Error information if the action fails.",
62	      "source": "=result.Error",
63	      "var": "error"
64	    }
65	  }
66	}
67	```
68	
69	`outputs.output` documents the success payload referenced downstream as `=js:$vars.{nodeId}.output`. `outputs.error` documents the failure shape; the runtime routes to the implicit `error` port when the action faults. See [Implicit error port on action nodes](file-format.md#implicit-error-port-on-action-nodes).
70	
71	> **For action nodes the instance `outputs` block is documentation, not the runtime contract.** What actually exposes the node's outputs as process-level `$vars.{nodeId}.output` is the matching `variables.nodes[]` entry — see [file-format.md — Node outputs](file-format.md#node-outputs). The BPMN emitter ignores the action-node instance `outputs` block at serialization (the manifest's `outputDefinition` drives the activity-side mapping). End / terminate nodes are the exception: their instance `outputs` block IS consumed to map workflow-level `out` variables. `uip maestro flow format` regenerates `variables.nodes[]` from the current node graph (MST-9972), so running format after structural edits self-heals an omitted entry.
72	
73	## Standard ports
74	
75	| Direction | Common name(s) | Notes |
76	| --- | --- | --- |
77	| Input (target) | `input` | Every action node accepts a single input edge on `input`. |
78	| Output (success, source) | `output`, `default`, or `success` | Name varies by plugin — `registry get` is authoritative. |
79	| Output (error, source) | `error` | Implicit on every action node via `outputs.error`. |
80	
81	Some plugins add dynamic source ports (e.g., HTTP `branch-{id}` from `inputs.branches`); those are documented in the plugin's own `impl.md`.
82	
83	## Adding and editing procedures
84	
85	For step-by-step add, delete, and wiring instructions, see [editing-operations.md](../author/references/editing-operations.md) and the JSON recipes in [editing-operations-json.md](../author/references/editing-operations-json.md). Plugin `impl.md` files describe only the inputs and wiring patterns that are specific to the node type.
86	
87	## Migrating a plugin to reference this template
88	
89	When converting an existing plugin `impl.md` to use this template:
90	
91	- **Keep in the plugin:** registry type string, `typeVersion`, plugin-specific input fields, plugin-specific configuration workflow (e.g., `node configure` for HTTP/connector nodes), plugin-specific rules, common patterns, debug table.
92	- **Replace with a link here:** generic JSON skeleton, generic `outputs` block (`=result.response` / `=result.Error`), generic registry-validation prose, generic "Adding / Editing" cross-reference.
93
